increment: Audited executor_pool at the pool sizes that break the monitor watching it. It inherits the ceiling - an all-benign 50-worker round is refused with the default monitor - but the real finding was elsewhere: THE INSTRUMENT RUN 385 ADDED TO CATCH A MISCALIBRATION WAS ITSELF MISCALIBRATED, TWICE. Defect 1, the assumed corpus: noise_margin_sigma is computed from benign_signal_mean=0.05 while executor_pool's workers emit 0.02, so a 20-worker all-benign round reported sigma -0.37 and below_floor=True while the real score was 0.40, under half the threshold - crying wolf at k=20 when the true ceiling was k=45. Defect 2, the wrong line: the margin measured self.cohort_threshold while round_verdict gated on effective_threshold, so with run 385's OWN adaptive threshold on it reported 'below the noise floor' at k=50 and k=100 while the gate sat 3 sigma clear. THREE INSTANCES ACROSS TWO RUNS, ONE SHAPE: a quantity computed from a constant the surrounding system had already moved. Structural cause - each fix adds a derived quantity, and a derived quantity is a new place for an assumption to hide. wiring-recreates-the-bug and instance-not-the-class arriving together at shorter range than either was seen at before: same file, same fix. Defect 2 is fixed and now yields a self-consistency property (with adaptive on the margin returns adaptive_z exactly, pinned at k=100). Defect 1 CANNOT be fixed the obvious way and the node says so: this class cannot estimate the benign floor from signals it sees, because separating benign from attack signal is the thing it is doing, and the median is contaminated by design under the fragmentation threat model. So the median only detects DISAGREEMENT with the assumption, and a contradicted margin is reported UNVALIDATED rather than as a number. executor_pool still refuses on abort - safe side - but now reports decision_basis evidence vs unreliable_monitor. cohort_monitor 17 -> 27 checks. +1 node, +6 edges.
